survey:front-matter.dimension: Front matter and document setup of papers/cardiac-rings/paper/cardiac-rings.tex, compared with the seven released LaTeX papers (minimal-winding, collapse-without-rotation, stable-expansion, rank-window, hh-dynamics, double-pendulum, nf-pulse) and with hh-pulse where it applies. Line numbers are from the working file as of this audit; another agent is editing it, so they may shift.

findings.location: End matter, between the end of the Discussion (line 797) and \textbf{Funding.} (line 800). Also the Labels paragraph (line 76).
findings.observed: There is no Data availability paragraph. The manuscript never names its companion repository (papers.json "companion": "ChaseHendrick/cardiac-rings") or a Zenodo DOI. A grep for github, zenodo, companion, doi.org or availab in the .tex finds nothing. The only place the programs are located is Section 8, which points into GENChase (see FM-2).
findings.convention: Six released LaTeX papers end with a {\raggedright\noindent\textbf{Data availability.} ...\par} paragraph that gives the companion URL and the Zenodo concept DOI: minimal-winding.tex:976, collapse-without-rotation.tex:570, stable-expansion.tex:313, hh-dynamics.tex:1013, double-pendulum.tex:463, nf-pulse.tex:843. rank-window note.tex:115 calls it 'Data and code availability'. hh-pulse paper.md:363-365 gives the companion and the concept DOI in its Reproducibility section. docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md section 1, step 5, is written rule: 'Put the version DOI in the paper's data availability paragraph'. hh-dynamics.tex:403 and nf-pulse.tex:97 also say in the Labels paragraph that paths name files of the folder that accompanies the paper, 'the companion repository named under Data availability'.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a paragraph before Funding, modelled on hh-dynamics.tex:1013. It should say that the programs (code/, with requirements), the records (data/) and the in-project reviews (review/) are in the companion repository https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/cardiac-rings, whose releases are archived on Zenodo, and leave the concept DOI to be filled at the first release. In the Labels paragraph, add the nf-pulse sentence that paths such as code/fourier/existence.py name files of the folder that accompanies the paper.

findings.location: Line 2 (header comment), line 223 (TODO comment), line 770 (Section 8 'Reproducibility and trust base', first paragraph), line 790 (Limitations, 'How far the background sources were read'), line 791 (Limitations, 'Searches').
findings.observed: The text and comments contain research/cardiac-cycle-certificates/ paths and send readers to them: 'in the layout of their canonical location \file{research/cardiac-cycle-certificates/} of the GENChase repository' (770), and 'The notes in \file{research/cardiac-cycle-certificates/notes/} of the GENChase repository record each reading' (790, and the same at 791). Running `node tools/paper-check.js --paper cardiac-rings` reports 'companion ChaseHendrick/cardiac-rings: paper/cardiac-rings.tex: a research/ or papers/ path of the GENChase repository (fix before "ready")'. The same note appears for README.md, code/run_all.sh, code/fourier/LEMMAS-stability.md and review/*, which belong to other audit dimensions.
findings.convention: tools/paper-sync.js INTERNAL refuses a research/ or papers/ path in any public file, and paper-check turns that into a failure from status 'ready' on. docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md, opening section: 'This repository may be private, so a paper never sends readers here.' None of the seven released LaTeX sources contains a research/ path (grep). nf-pulse.tex:97 names the GENChase repository only to explain where commit hashes come from, and points readers to the companion for every file.
findings.proposed_fix: Say that code/ and data/ are folders of the companion, and that the records' hashes refer to paths relative to the paper's folder. Either ship the reading and search logs in review/ and cite them there, or state the reading basis without a path. Remove the research/ path from the line 1-2 comment and from the TODO block (see FM-9). Afterwards, check that paper-check no longer lists paper/cardiac-rings.tex.

findings.location: Line 776, Section 8, paragraph 'What is certified, and reruns.'
findings.observed: The paper cites \file{notes/rerun-2026-10-01.md} as the record of the 2026-10-01 rerun. The companion does not carry notes/: tools/paper-sync.js PRIVATE_DIRS is ['notes/', 'submission/']. A reader of the preprint is therefore pointed at a file they cannot obtain.
findings.convention: docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md section 0: 'notes/ stays in GENChase; the companion does not carry it.' nf-pulse keeps its in-project checks under review/ and ext/*/REPORT.md and cites them there (nf-pulse.tex:819). No other released LaTeX paper cites a file under notes/. hh-dynamics.tex:1006 says its readings are 'in the folder notes/ of the companion repository', which the sync does not carry either: that is the same defect in a released paper, not a convention to copy.
findings.proposed_fix: Put the rerun record in a folder the companion carries, for example review/rerun-2026-10-01.md or data/, and cite it there. Keep notes/ for the quality record only.

findings.location: Labels paragraph, line 76. Lemma 6.1 (lem:link), line 733. Remark 3.1 (rem:same), line 188. Proposition 4.4, line 265. Corollaries 5.4 and 5.6, lines 523 and 538. thmx Theorems 5.3, 5.15 and 5.17, lines 511, 657 and 694. Appendix Proposition A.4 and Theorems A.5 and A.7, lines 956 and 992.
findings.observed: The Labels paragraph says 'The lemmas are proved here' and that the theorems' inequalities are 'decided in interval or ball arithmetic'. Lemma 6.1 is computer-assisted, not proved: its proof rests on code/fourier/link_cell.py, which checks 14 block inequalities in exact rational arithmetic with integer square-root bounds ('All 14 checks pass', data/link_cell.txt). Theorem A(iii) rests on this lemma, so 'interval or ball arithmetic' is also inaccurate. The Labels paragraph names only Theorems A-C, 'the lemmas' and the appendix 'facts'. Proposition 4.4, Corollaries 5.4 and 5.6, Theorems 5.3, 5.15 and 5.17, and the appendix Proposition and Theorems carry no label anywhere. Remark 3.1 reports interval enclosures from 'a separate CAPD pipeline that is not part of these proofs' and has no label in its header; only its last sentence calls it a consistency check. QUALITY.md item 3 is checked [x] on the strength of this paragraph.
findings.convention: Quality bar item 3 (notes/QUALITY.md; tools/paper-check.js BAR 'Every claim labelled') requires that each result is labelled proved, computer-assisted, formal or numerical in the paper. The three computer-assisted papers released since hh-dynamics put a label on every result: hh-dynamics.tex:403 ('Every result carries a label', defining Proved, Computer-assisted, Cited and Numerical) with [proved]/[computer-assisted] in every header from 427 to 870; nf-pulse.tex:97 ('Every result carries one label'), with headers such as 'computer-assisted: \file{code/certify_rest.py}, check~1' at 154; double-pendulum.tex:71 ('Every statement is labelled') with headers from 81 to 414. The older vortex papers do it differently: collapse-without-rotation.tex:66 lists the proved results in a sentence of the introduction, and minimal-winding and stable-expansion label in the text. The released papers disagree on the form, but each of them labels every result. The new Remark rem:phase (line 756, '[phase reduction; numerical, not part of the proofs]') already follows the header form.
findings.proposed_fix: Give Lemma 6.1 the header '[the two cell certificates enclose the same orbit; computer-assisted: code/fourier/link_cell.py, data/link_cell.txt]'. Put [proved] on the lemmas, propositions, corollaries and thmx theorems, including the appendix and the new every-N lemmas (lem:tailT to lem:glue). Label Remark 3.1 in its header as a consistency check not used in any proof. Rewrite the Labels paragraph after nf-pulse.tex:97: define Proved, Computer-assisted and Numerical, say 'interval, ball or exact rational arithmetic', and say that numerical results are labelled where they appear and collected in Section 7. Update QUALITY.md item 3 to match.

findings.location: Preamble lines 19-23 (\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}, \renewcommand{\thetheorem}{\Alph{theorem}}, \newtheorem{thmx}[lemma]{Theorem}). Theorems A-C at lines 129, 143 and 192. Appendix A at lines 876-878 with thmx at 956 and 992. TODO at line 225.
findings.observed: The paper's own main results are lettered: Theorems A, B and C, with Theorems D and E planned in the TODO at line 225. A second environment also prints 'Theorem', numbered with the lemma counter: Theorems 5.3, 5.15 and 5.17 in the PDF, and Theorems A.5 and A.7 in Appendix A. So 'Theorem A' (the cell) sits next to 'Theorem A.5' and 'Lemma A.1' (Appendix A), and QUALITY.md cites both 'Theorems A and B' and 'Theorem A.5(ii)'.
findings.convention: All seven released LaTeX papers number their own theorems with arabic numerals through one \newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}: minimal-winding.tex:20, collapse-without-rotation.tex:19, stable-expansion.tex:17, hh-dynamics.tex:22, double-pendulum.tex:20, nf-pulse.tex:21 (rank-window has no theorems). Only hh-dynamics uses letters, and only for cited theorems, with the stated reason (hh-dynamics.tex:27-29): 'The two cited theorems are lettered: H (Andronov-Hopf) and K (Krawczyk), so that they are not confused with the numbered results of this paper.' No released paper has two environments that both print 'Theorem' for its own results.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop \renewcommand{\thetheorem}{\Alph{theorem}}, so that the main results become Theorems 1-3 and the G_Ks results 4-5. Either rename the thmx results (Hill sectors, the certificate, the conclusion, the appendix facts) to Proposition, sharing the lemma counter, or number them in the main Theorem series. Update the cross-references in README.md, notes/QUALITY.md and papers.json at the same time.

findings.location: Line 45, \date{Draft of October 1, 2026}. In the PDF: title page, line 10 of pdftotext output.
findings.observed: The title page prints 'Draft of October 1, 2026'. The date is also stale: the source records that Appendix A was 'added on 2026-10-02' (Limitations, line 789).
findings.convention: All seven released LaTeX sources have \date{}: collapse-without-rotation.tex:41, double-pendulum.tex:38, hh-dynamics.tex:373, minimal-winding.tex:41, nf-pulse.tex:49, rank-window note.tex:33, stable-expansion.tex:34. The release notes record the removal: collapse-without-rotation/RELEASES.md:8, stable-expansion/RELEASES.md:8 and double-pendulum/RELEASES.md:7 each say 'The title-page date line is removed.'
findings.proposed_fix: Set \date{}. Draft status belongs in papers.json and the README, not on the title page.

findings.location: Header comment, lines 1-2. Committed papers/cardiac-rings/paper/cardiac-rings.pdf. Also README.md:7 and :123, and the papers.json note.
findings.observed: The header comment does not say how the PDF is built. pdfinfo shows the committed PDF was made by 'Producer: pdfTeX-1.40.25' (CreationDate 2026-10-01 23:30 UTC). The PDF predates completed parts of the source: it has no Appendix A, although the Labels paragraph (76) and the Limitations item (789) cite Appendix A. README and papers.json say 'built with pdflatex' and '26 pages'.
findings.convention: Every released LaTeX source says on its first lines how its PDF is built. minimal-winding.tex:1, collapse-without-rotation.tex:1 and stable-expansion.tex:1 say 'built with Tectonic (tectonic <id>.tex)'. hh-dynamics.tex:1-2, double-pendulum.tex:1-2, nf-pulse.tex:1 and rank-window note.tex:1 say 'pdflatex, run three times', so the comments disagree. But pdfinfo shows 'Producer: xdvipdfmx (0.1)' for all eight committed released PDFs. Their 2026-09-29 figure reviews record builds with PAPER_PDF_ENGINE=tectonic (for example double-pendulum/notes/figures-2026-09-29.md:13 and minimal-winding/notes/FIGURE-REVIEW-2026-09-29.md:7).
findings.proposed_fix: Begin the file with '% The manuscript; cardiac-rings.pdf beside it is this file built with Tectonic (PAPER_PDF_ENGINE=tectonic sh tools/paper-build.sh cardiac-rings).' When the current edits land, rebuild with Tectonic, and update the page count and engine in README.md, the papers.json note and QUALITY.md item 7.

findings.location: thebibliography at line 806, \appendix at line 876, Section A (app:resolvent) at line 878, \end{document} at line 1000.
findings.observed: Appendix A follows the bibliography, so the document does not end with its references.
findings.convention: Every released LaTeX source ends with thebibliography immediately before \end{document} (minimal-winding 985/1076, collapse-without-rotation 579/620, stable-expansion 523/563, hh-dynamics 1021/1104, double-pendulum 470/548, nf-pulse 851/940, rank-window 124/151). The two released papers with appendices put them before the references: stable-expansion.tex has \appendix at 323 after its end-matter statements (313-321) and before thebibliography at 523; hh-pulse paper.md has Appendices A-C at 383-497 before '## References' at 522.
findings.proposed_fix: Move \appendix and Section A before thebibliography, in the stable-expansion order: Discussion, then Data availability/Funding/Use of AI/Rights, then \appendix, then the references.

findings.location: Comment blocks at lines 222-230 ('% TODO (integration pending; not printed): ...') and 785-786.
findings.observed: The source carries planning notes for the G_Ks branch and the Hopf bridge. They name research/ paths, notes/QUALITY.md, planned 'Theorems D and E' and the renaming of the study's 'Theorem C'. paper-sync copies paper/ verbatim, so these comments would ship in the public companion's .tex.
findings.convention: A grep for TODO, FIXME or 'pending' in comments finds nothing in the seven released LaTeX sources. Their comments only describe the build, the figure scripts and the generated blocks (for example hh-dynamics.tex:1-4 and 'BEGIN generated by code/hh_make_numbers.py').
findings.proposed_fix: Move the integration plan to notes/ (QUALITY.md or a plan file) before any release, and keep only build and provenance comments in the manuscript.

findings.location: Preamble (no graphicx), whole document. There is no paper/figures/ folder.
findings.observed: The manuscript has no figure: zero \includegraphics and no graphicx package. It has four tables.
findings.convention: Every released paper has at least one figure: minimal-winding (3 \includegraphics), collapse-without-rotation (1), stable-expansion (1), hh-dynamics (3), double-pendulum (1), nf-pulse (1), rank-window results.tex (3), hh-pulse paper.md:148 (1). Each has a paper/figures/ folder, and the figure scripts are named in the header comment (for example minimal-winding.tex:1-3). Several are labelled numerical illustrations of the proved object: hh-pulse pulse-profiles, nf-pulse pulse-profile, hh-dynamics orbits. This is a uniform practice, not a written rule.
findings.proposed_fix: Consider one figure, labelled a numerical illustration: for example the voltage component of the cell orbit and of a ring wave's profile from the stored centers, or the ring spectrum near the axis. Draw it with a script in code/ named in the header comment, and follow the figure rules of docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md section 0 (legends outside the data panels).

findings.location: Abstract, line 55: '\textbf{MSC 2020:} 37C27, 34C25, 65G20, 92C30, 37M20.'
findings.observed: 65G20 sits in the middle of the list.
findings.convention: Every released paper that lists 65G20 puts it last: minimal-winding.tex:53, stable-expansion.tex:44, hh-dynamics.tex:383, double-pendulum.tex:48, nf-pulse.tex:59.

findings.location: Abstract body, lines 50-52.
findings.observed: The LaTeX abstract body is about 3,046 characters (about 490 words) of source, the longest of all the manuscripts. The every-N material now being added accounts for part of the growth: the committed PDF's abstract still ends 'nothing is claimed for a continuum cable or for tissue'.
findings.convention: The released LaTeX abstract bodies run about 1,697 (nf-pulse), 1,898 (double-pendulum), 1,925 (hh-dynamics), 1,932 (minimal-winding), 2,268 (stable-expansion) and 2,835 (collapse-without-rotation) characters of source, so the released papers disagree; four stay near arXiv's limit. tools/paper-check.js enforces ABSTRACT_LIMIT = 1920 on the arXiv metadata abstract, and the README's '## Abstract' becomes the Zenodo description.
findings.proposed_fix: When the every-N sentences go in, condense the abstract, for example by shortening the method sentences on strip covers, aliasing and Schur complements, and keep the README abstract in step.

findings.location: Line 1 '% The manuscript (status: draft).' Discussion, line 797: 'an interval of $G_{Ks}$ (in progress)'.
findings.observed: Project-status wording appears in a source comment and in the printed Discussion.
findings.convention: Only double-pendulum.tex:3 carries a status, as a comment ('% Status: ready.'). No released manuscript prints project status in its text: nf-pulse.tex:831 'Open problems' and hh-dynamics.tex:1008 'Future work' state open questions without saying what is under way.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop '(in progress)' from the Discussion. Drop the status from the header comment, or keep it in step with papers.json at every status change.

findings.location: Section 8 heading, line 768: 'Reproducibility and trust base'.
findings.observed: The section title adds 'and trust base'.
findings.convention: hh-dynamics.tex:963 and nf-pulse.tex:771 title it 'Reproducibility', as does hh-pulse paper.md:361 ('7. Reproducibility'). Those two LaTeX papers put the trust base in a \paragraph{Trust base.} (hh-dynamics.tex:932, nf-pulse.tex:750).
findings.proposed_fix: Optionally retitle the section 'Reproducibility' and keep the trusted components as paragraphs, as the code already does.

checked_and_fine: Document class and options: \documentclass[11pt]{article} with geometry letterpaper and margin=1in, identical to all seven released LaTeX papers.

Fonts and encoding: T1 fontenc with lmodern; also amsmath, amssymb, amsthm, array, booktabs and microtype; \setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}; hyperref with hidelinks. xurl and \DeclareUrlCommand\file match nf-pulse.tex, and \file matches hh-dynamics.tex.

\hypersetup pdftitle equals the papers.json title and pdfauthor is 'Chase Hendrick'. `node tools/paper-check.js --paper cardiac-rings` (run with TMPDIR in the scratchpad) reports OK [draft] with no title or email problem; the PDF has 26 pages, letter size.

Title formatting: \title{\Large\bfseries ...\\ ...}, as in minimal-winding, collapse-without-rotation, hh-dynamics, nf-pulse and rank-window. stable-expansion and double-pendulum use a plain \title, so the released papers differ and cardiac-rings follows the majority.

Author block (lines 44-45): name, 'Independent Researcher', the mailto link to chase@hendrickresearch.com (equal to papers.json author.email) and ORCID 0009-0002-9754-6087, byte-identical to the seven released papers.

Abstract environment with \medskip, then \noindent\textbf{Keywords:} and \textbf{MSC 2020:} inside the abstract, as in the six released papers that have keywords. Keywords include 'computer-assisted proof' and the arithmetic used, as hh-dynamics and nf-pulse do.

Theorem setup apart from the lettering (FM-5): lemma numbered within section; proposition, corollary, definition and remark share it; definition style for remarks and definitions. This matches nf-pulse.tex:22-27 and hh-dynamics.tex:24-32.

The main theorems carry 'computer-assisted' in their headers, as hh-dynamics, double-pendulum and nf-pulse do. The new Remark rem:phase (line 756) is labelled '[phase reduction; numerical, not part of the proofs]' in its header.

The Labels paragraph is the last paragraph of the Introduction, as in hh-dynamics.tex:403 and nf-pulse.tex:97. Section 7, 'Numerical observations', opens by saying nothing in it is proved or used in a proof.

Section order: Introduction, model, Results, proofs (existence, stability, time domain), Numerical observations, Reproducibility, 'Limitations and what has been checked', Discussion. This matches nf-pulse (which adds Open problems) and hh-dynamics (which ends with Future work). Released papers disagree on a final Open problems section (minimal-winding, collapse-without-rotation and nf-pulse have one; stable-expansion and double-pendulum do not), so its absence is not a departure.

End-matter statements: \textbf{Funding.}, then \textbf{Use of AI.} with the exact wording and body size of the 2026-10-01 rule in docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md, then a Rights paragraph whose text is identical to hh-dynamics.tex:1019, nf-pulse.tex:849 and hh-pulse paper.md:518, in the same order as hh-dynamics and nf-pulse.

No claim of an outside review. The Limitations section says 'This is not an outside review' and 'None of these is an outside review', as nf-pulse.tex:819 and hh-dynamics.tex:1006 do, consistent with AGENTS.md.

The reading basis of sources not read in full is stated once, positively, in the Limitations section ('Known from abstracts: ...'), as the 2026-10-01 rule in docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md on sources that could not be obtained requires.
The bibliography is a hand-written thebibliography, as in all seven released LaTeX papers; the {99} width argument is cosmetic.

survey:end-matter.dimension: End matter and references of papers/cardiac-rings/paper/cardiac-rings.tex, compared with the eight released papers (minimal-winding, collapse-without-rotation, stable-expansion, rank-window, hh-dynamics, double-pendulum, nf-pulse, hh-pulse) and the rules in AGENTS.md, docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md, papers/papers.json, tools/paper-check.js and tools/paper-sync.js. Another agent was editing the file while I read it, so line numbers are those of my last read (1000 lines). I ran only `node tools/paper-check.js --paper cardiac-rings`, with TMPDIR set to the scratchpad.

findings.location: End matter, lines 798-804 (\medskip, Funding, Use of AI, Rights); also Section 9 'Reproducibility and trust base', lines 768-770
findings.observed: There is no Data availability paragraph. The manuscript never gives the companion URL or any DOI: a grep finds no 'github.com/ChaseHendrick', no 'zenodo' and no 'availability'. Section 9 sends the reader to code/ and data/ 'in the layout of their canonical location ... of the GENChase repository' but does not say where those folders can be downloaded. A reader of the PDF on Zenodo or arXiv cannot find the programs the theorems rest on.
findings.convention: All eight released papers name their companion repository and its Zenodo concept DOI. Seven do it in a labelled paragraph that opens the end matter, after \medskip, as {\raggedright\noindent\textbf{Data availability.} ...\par}: minimal-winding.tex:976, collapse-without-rotation.tex:570, stable-expansion.tex:313, hh-dynamics.tex:1013, double-pendulum.tex:463, nf-pulse.tex:843, and rank-window/paper/note.tex:115, which titles it 'Data and code availability'. hh-pulse/paper/paper.md:363-365 does it inside its Section 7 'Reproducibility'. The written rules: docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md lines 7-8 ('a paper never sends readers here'), line ~37 ('The paper then cites a DOI for the exact programs it used') and Section 1, step 5 ('Put the version DOI in the paper's data availability paragraph'). Those rules assume the paragraph exists. papers.json gives the companion as ChaseHendrick/cardiac-rings, with codeDoi null.
findings.proposed_fix: Insert before Funding, keeping the \medskip above it, in the hh-dynamics/nf-pulse form: "{\raggedright\noindent\textbf{Data availability.} The programs of this paper and their output are in its folder: the programs in \texttt{code/} (with \texttt{code/requirements.txt} and \texttt{code/run\_all.sh}), the stored records on which the theorems rest in \texttt{data/}, and the project's checks in \texttt{review/}. These files are available in the companion repository, \url{https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/cardiac-rings}, whose releases are archived on Zenodo under the concept DOI \url{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.NNNNNNNN}.\par}". The concept DOI does not exist until Zenodo archives release 1.0.0, so that release needs a sentence that is already true, not a literal placeholder. paper-check.js scans only the arXiv metadata and the cover letter for '[...]' holes, not the .tex, so a fake DOI or an 'XXXX' would ship unnoticed. Precedents for the pre-DOI wording: hh-dynamics before commit c68cd4a ('..., \url{https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/hh-dynamics}, whose release 1.0.1 is to hold this version') and nf-pulse before c68cd4a ('A public release of that folder with an archived DOI is planned before submission'). Use for example '..., \url{https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/cardiac-rings}, whose release 1.0.0 is to hold this version.' After Zenodo archives 1.0.0, put in the DOI, set codeDoi and archiveVersion in papers.json, and make release 1.0.1 so that the archived PDF carries the DOI (PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md, Section 1, step 5).

findings.location: Line 2 (header comment); line 770 (Section 9, first paragraph); line 776 (\file{notes/rerun-2026-10-01.md}); line 790 (end of 'How far the background sources were read'); line 791 ('Searches')
findings.observed: The manuscript sends readers to places the companion will not contain. Lines 2, 770, 790 and 791 name 'research/cardiac-cycle-certificates/...' of the GENChase repository. Line 776 cites notes/rerun-2026-10-01.md, but notes/ is in PRIVATE_DIRS (tools/paper-sync.js:26), so it is not published. `node tools/paper-check.js --paper cardiac-rings` already reports 'companion ChaseHendrick/cardiac-rings: paper/cardiac-rings.tex: a research/ or papers/ path of the GENChase repository (fix before "ready")'. At status ready this becomes a failure. The record of the readings and of the prior-article searches, which is what the paper gives as the basis of its reading statements and its novelty sentence, is therefore out of the reader's reach.
findings.convention: docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md:7: 'This repository may be private, so a paper never sends readers here.' tools/paper-sync.js:29-31 rejects research/ and papers/ paths in staged files. nf-pulse.tex:97 explains that GENChase is not part of the companion and names only non-research paths and commits of it. nf-pulse keeps its reruns in review/RERUNS.md (nf-pulse.tex:794) and its searches in review/PRIOR-ART.md and review/lead/priorart/PRIORART.md (nf-pulse.tex:95), all of which ship. hh-pulse puts its search in Appendix C (paper.md:497-514), and hh-dynamics states its searches in the text. Do not copy hh-dynamics.tex:1006: it points to 'notes/ of the companion repository', which paper-sync also leaves out.
findings.proposed_fix: Copy research/cardiac-cycle-certificates/notes/prior-article-rings-2026-10-01.md and readings-rings-2026-10-01.md into a shipped folder, for example review/, and cite those paths at lines 790 and 791. Alternatively, summarize the searches in an appendix as hh-pulse does. Move or copy notes/rerun-2026-10-01.md to review/ (compare nf-pulse review/RERUNS.md) and cite it there at line 776. Check the copies for research/ paths and email addresses, which paper-sync also rejects. Rewrite line 770 without the literal path, after nf-pulse.tex:97, for example: 'The programs were developed in the GENChase repository, which is not part of the companion; \file{code/} and \file{data/} keep the layout of that folder, whose paths the records name.' Replace the header comment with the released form, for example '% The manuscript; cardiac-rings.pdf beside it is this file built with pdflatex, run three times (sh tools/paper-build.sh cardiac-rings).' (hh-dynamics.tex:1, double-pendulum.tex:1-2).

findings.location: Line 491 ('see also Kato's book \cite[Ch.~III, Sect.~6]{kato1976}'), line 880 (Appendix A intro, the same pinpoint), line 856 (\bibitem{kato1976}), line 790 (the reading list, which leaves Kato out)
findings.observed: Kato is cited twice with a chapter and section, but the paper never says what that rests on. papers/cardiac-rings/notes/QUALITY.md, item 4 (lines 83-85), says the book 'has still not been checked against a copy'. The reading-basis list at line 790 covers every other background work, but not kato1976 (nor johansson2017 or capd2021, which are cited only as software). A pinpoint into an unread book suggests a reading that did not take place. The entry also has no doi:, although every other book in the list has one (gss1988, hi1997).

Apache-2.0, subject to component notices ...\par} form of hh-dynamics:1019 and nf-pulse:849, and to hh-pulse:518 in Markdown. Hendrick, <title>, preprint (2026); programs and data archived on Zenodo, concept doi:10.5281/zenodo.<n>, at \url{https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/<id>}.'

(line 72), and the plain 'Known from abstracts / its title and ... account / metadata or a table of contents / excerpts of its abstract' list at line 790. Ermentrout's pinpoint \cite[Theorem~3.1 and Lemma~3.2]{ermentrout1992} in the new remark falls inside the pages read (pp. 1674-1677, line 790; RESEARCH.md:2209). The new vblm2010 entry follows the list's format, is sorted under V, and has its reading basis ('Known from abstracts').

findings.location: Title at lines 16 and 43. The same title is in README.md:1, papers/papers.json:191 and notes/QUALITY.md:1.
findings.observed: The title reads "Stable Rotating Waves in Rings of a Modified Ventricular Myocyte Model Near a Hopf Point: Computer-Assisted Proofs in Fourier Space". This version proves nothing about a Hopf point. The value G_Ks = 0.0275 is 1.46% below a Hopf point that Erhardt computed numerically (lines 60-62). The paper itself says that the identification with the Hopf branch is numerical (abstract, line 51) and supported by numerics only (line 784). The "Hopf bridge" exists only as a TODO comment (lines 222-230). The subtitle "in Fourier Space" also does not cover Theorem A(i), which is a time-domain proof with CAPD (lines 132 and 721-731). "Myocyte" appears only in the title; the body says "cell model" throughout. The title is identical in every source: the tex \title, pdftitle, the README, papers.json, QUALITY.md and the PDF metadata (pdfinfo). paper-check reports OK.
findings.convention: The released titles name only what is proved. nf-pulse is "...: Computer-Assisted Existence and Spectral Stability" and names the weaker stability it proves (nf-pulse.tex:47). hh-dynamics is "Hopf Bifurcations and Bistability ... at the 1952 Parameters: Computer-Assisted Proofs" (hh-dynamics.tex:371), and there the Hopf points are proved (Theorem thm:hopf). hh-pulse is "...: A Computer-Assisted Existence Proof" (paper.md:2).
findings.proposed_fix: For this version, drop "Near a Hopf Point" and "in Fourier Space". One option is "Stable Rotating Waves in Rings of a Modified Ventricular Cell Model: Computer-Assisted Proofs", or name the parameter as hh-dynamics does ("... at G_Ks = 0.0275"). Keep the Hopf wording only if the Hopf bridge is integrated as a theorem. Change the tex \title and pdftitle, README.md:1, papers.json:191 and QUALITY.md:1 together so that paper-check stays green. MSC 37M20 (line 55) belongs to the same Hopf framing and can go with it.

findings.location: Abstract, line 51 ("two computer-assisted proofs, sharing no library"); line 68 ("The two proofs share no library"); README.md:17.
findings.observed: The paper claims that the two cell proofs share no library. The CAPD route trusts "filib and MPFR" (line 774), and its MPFR build needs GMP (README.md: CAPD "built with multiprecision (GMP and MPFR)"). The pinned python-flint 0.9.0 wheel bundles libflint, libgmp 6.3.0 and libmpfr 4.2.2 (python_flint.libs/ in the installed package). Both routes therefore link GMP and MPFR. The claim is literally false, and it overstates how independent the two proofs are, in the abstract.
findings.convention: The released papers state their trust bases without overstatement. hh-dynamics.tex:932 ("Trust base") and nf-pulse.tex:750 name each library they rely on, and double-pendulum.tex:461 ("What the proof trusts") does the same.
findings.proposed_fix: Write, for example, "two independent computer-assisted proofs, with different methods and interval libraries (CAPD with filib and MPFR; Arb)". Add one sentence in Section 8 saying that both link GMP and MPFR.

findings.location: Line 76 (\paragraph{Labels.}: "The lemmas are proved here"); Lemma 6.1, lem:link, lines 733-739; Lemma 4.8, lem:real, line 359.
findings.observed: Lemma 6.1 is established by a program. Its proof runs code/fourier/link_cell.py in exact rationals ("All 14 checks pass ... a control with every radius divided by 10 fails"). The Labels paragraph nevertheless puts it among the lemmas that are "proved here", that is, without computation. The proof of Lemma 4.8 also uses a computation: it ends "$\omega_* \ge \bar\omega - r_{\mathrm{ex}} > 0$ is checked in Arb". Only Theorems A to C carry a label in their headers.
findings.convention: "Proved" means no computation. hh-dynamics.tex:403 defines it as "a written proof in this paper, with no computation", and nf-pulse.tex:97 uses the same definition. Each result that uses a program says so in its header, for example nf-pulse.tex:154 (\begin{lemma}[computer-assisted: \file{code/certify_rest.py} ...]), nf-pulse.tex:344 ([proved; its hypotheses are checked by ...]) and hh-dynamics.tex:451 ([computer-assisted]). Quality-bar item 3 of notes/QUALITY.md requires every claim to be labelled correctly.
findings.proposed_fix: Label Lemma 6.1 in its header, for example [computer-assisted: \file{code/fourier/link_cell.py}, exact rationals]. Move the positivity check of omega in Lemma 4.8 into its hypotheses, which the proof of Theorem B already checks, or label that lemma too. Rewrite the Labels paragraph so that it names the computer-assisted lemmas.

findings.location: Line 74 (\paragraph{Novelty.}); line 72 (Di Marco et al.); line 790 ("Known from excerpts of its abstract: Di Marco et al.").
findings.observed: The priority sentence is "no earlier computer-assisted proof of a rotating wave in a ring of diffusively coupled cells". Di Marco, Forti, Garay, Koller and Pancioni (JMAA 2016) treat Floquet multipliers of a rotating wave in a ring network, and their paper is known only from search-engine snippets of its abstract (research/cardiac-cycle-certificates/notes/readings-rings-2026-10-01.md:106-108: "NOT the full text and NOT the verbatim abstract"). The priority sentence carries no scope for that paper. The ledger set conditions on this wording: RESEARCH.md:2228 says "Before any priority wording, read ... Di Marco et al.", and RESEARCH.md:2245 says "Read the full text of Di Marco et al. before submission". The full text has not been read.
findings.convention: docs/PUBLISHING-PAPERS.md:191-196: for a source that could not be obtained, "keep any priority limitation that depends on it as a scope statement ('as far as the abstract describes it')". hh-dynamics.tex:401 does this for Du and Hassard: "neither their abstract nor the review in zbMATH mentions ...", and it claims no priority where that source may contain the result. nf-pulse.tex:95 names the works known only in part.
findings.proposed_fix: Either read the full text of Di Marco et al. and record the reading in the ledger, or scope the sentence. For example: "... and, as far as the abstract excerpts of Di Marco et al. describe their method, none of a rotating wave in a ring of diffusively coupled cells".

The same paper says "(abstract)" when it quotes Troy 1976.

findings.location: Abstract, line 51 ("The identification of these orbits with the Hopf branch is numerical"); line 784 ("is supported by numerics only"); line 751.
findings.observed: No numerical continuation of the branch from Erhardt's Hopf point to G_Ks = 0.0275 is reported. code/numerics/hopf_and_orbit.py (docstring, lines 1-6) and data/numerics-hopf-orbit.json compute only the equilibrium, the Hopf point and the cycle at 0.0275. The identification therefore rests on three things: the Hopf point lies 1.46% away, the period is close to the Hopf period, and the amplitude is small. The ledger calls it an inference (RESEARCH.md:2208: "that identification is an inference").
findings.convention: Every claim carries its true basis. nf-pulse.tex:97 and hh-dynamics.tex:403 label numerical results "floating-point or high-precision computation". Inferences are not presented as computations.
findings.proposed_fix: Write, for example: "That these orbits lie on the branch born at Erhardt's Hopf point is an inference from numerical evidence (parameter distance 1.46%, period 53.59 against 52.65 ms, small amplitude); no branch was continued." Use the same wording in the abstract, line 784 and the README.

findings.convention: nf-pulse.tex:97: numerical results "are labelled where they appear". QUALITY.md bar item 3: "numerical results are never stated as theorems" and every claim is labelled.
findings.proposed_fix: Write "the floating-point leading exponent (Section 7) is about ...".
